title: Pilot rollout checklist — Provision-to-ready automation (staging → prod)
linked_artifacts: Linear: ENG-2759 (SLA for ‘ready’ marking in control plane)
GitHub: redwood/pr-48245 (Fix race: Ready set before perf-canary)
content:
Context
- This is the step-by-step checklist for piloting the new “provision-to-ready” automation pipeline for Dedicated capacity.
- Goals of the pilot:
  - Prove end-to-end automation works across the full lifecycle (Requested → Provisioning → Imaging → Bootstrapping → Validating → Ready).
  - Validate readiness gates + perf-canary; ensure routing only consumes Ready capacity.
  - Verify dashboards/alerts and oncall usability.
- Scope: staging pilot first, then production pilot on a small internal pool and a controlled customer expansion window.

Owners / on-point
- Infra on-point (pilot execution): Harish Reddy
- Sprint eng lead (fleet automation): Vanessa Ortiz
- SRE on-point (rollout safety/paging decisions): Rafael Mendes
- Release coordinator / change window: Connor O’Brien
- Control plane / ready state verification: Ethan Park
- Dashboards/metrics verification: Aisha Bello
- Runbook updates / operator comms: Kira Thompson

Definitions (quick)
- “Provisioned”: infra exists (nodes/network/IAM/cluster created) but not safe for routing.
- “Ready”: all readiness gates passed + perf-canary passed + control plane state transitioned to Ready + routing advertises capacity.
- “Break-glass”: audited override for config validation only (NOT a bypass for readiness gates). If used, must log reason + follow-up ticket.

Pre-flight checklist (do before any pilot run)
1) Change window + comms set
   - [ ] Confirm planned staging window (date/time) in #eng-infra.
   - [ ] Confirm production pilot window with #eng-releases and #eng-oncall.
   - [ ] If customer pilot: confirm CS/Sales comms plan + maintenance window in SUP ticket and email thread.
   - [ ] Ensure an “abort by” time is agreed (e.g., T+90m from start) so we don’t drift into peak traffic.

2) Code + config readiness
   - [ ] Feature flag state confirmed:
     - Staging: provisioning_pipeline_v2 = ON
     - Production: provisioning_pipeline_v2 = OFF (until prod pilot step)
   - [ ] Operator CLI version is current in staging jumpbox/tooling environment.
   - [ ] Terraform module version pinned for the pilot pool (do not float to latest mid-run).
   - [ ] Golden image version for target SKU/region confirmed, signed, and listed in compatibility matrix.
   - [ ] Pool config passes schema validation (run local lint first).

3) Access + permissions
   - [ ] Verify pilot operators have permissions to:
     - trigger provisioning runs
     - pause/resume
     - re-run stages
     - view logs/metrics dashboards
   - [ ] Verify break-glass admins list (who can override validation) and oncall contact.

4) Observability checks
   - [ ] Dedicated readiness dashboard loads and filters work for pool_id/customer_id/region.
   - [ ] time_to_ready metrics present in staging (overall + per-stage histograms).
   - [ ] Alerting is set to ticket-only for staging (no paging) unless otherwise agreed.
   - [ ] Correlation ID is present in logs for each stage start/finish.

5) Rollback readiness (confirm before starting)
   - [ ] Rollback steps are understood and explicitly assigned:
     - Disable feature flag
     - Pause any in-flight provisioning runs
     - Ensure routing does not advertise the pool
     - Revert to manual provisioning procedure if needed
   - [ ] “Stop the bleeding” action confirmed: force pool to NOT READY in control plane if any doubt.

================================================================================
STAGING PILOT (internal pool)

Target: 1 internal staging pool creation or expansion
- Pool: <staging_pool_id>
- Region/SKU: <region> / <gpu_sku>
- Expected run time (budget): <X> minutes (see stage budgets)

A) Announce start + set context
1) [ ] Post in #eng-infra:
   - “Starting staging pilot for provision-to-ready automation; pool=<id>, region=<r>, sku=<s>. On-point: Harish + Vanessa + Rafael. Dashboard link: <url>. Correlation ID will be posted when run starts.”
2) [ ] Create/confirm tracking comment on ENG-2752 with timestamp and links.

B) Run a dry-run / plan validation
3) [ ] Run CLI dry-run (no mutations). Capture output in ENG-2752.
   - Example:
     - rwctl fleet provision run --env=staging --pool=<id> --dry-run
   - Verify:
     - Terraform plan looks reasonable
     - image version resolves
     - config validation passes
     - expected outputs include cluster_id/nodegroup ids

C) Start the provisioning run
4) [ ] Trigger run (mutating) and record correlation_id.
   - rwctl fleet provision run --env=staging --pool=<id>
5) [ ] Post correlation_id in #eng-infra thread + paste dashboard deep link.

D) Stage-by-stage verification (do not just “wait for Ready”)
6) Provisioning stage
   - [ ] Terraform apply started (event emitted)
   - [ ] No repeated IAM/quota errors (if present, follow rollback criteria below)
   - [ ] Stage duration within budget; if not, note cause

7) Imaging stage
   - [ ] Nodes pull golden image successfully
   - [ ] If imaging is slow, verify artifact mirror availability in-region
   - [ ] If imaging timeouts occur, confirm fallback behavior (alternate mirror/prewarm) or stop

8) Bootstrapping stage
   - [ ] Cluster comes up; runtime/k8s components installed
   - [ ] Helm values are correct for this pool (common failure mode: wrong values file)
   - [ ] No repeated bootstrap retries that suggest non-idempotent behavior

9) Validating stage
   - [ ] GPU health checks pass (no ECC error threshold exceeded)
   - [ ] Networking checks pass (DNS/TLS/egress)
   - [ ] Runtime smoke test passes

10) Perf-canary readiness suite
   - [ ] Perf-canary run started only after validation prerequisites
   - [ ] Perf-canary output is stored/linked (pass/fail + summary)
   - [ ] Confirm race-condition fix behavior: Ready MUST NOT set before perf-canary completion

11) Ready state + routing
   - [ ] Control plane state transitions to Ready
   - [ ] Routing advertises pool only after Ready
   - [ ] Verify “Validating” is NOT treated as usable capacity

E) Post-run validation (staging)
12) [ ] Verify time-to-ready metric breakdown aligns with observed timestamps.
13) [ ] Ensure events are searchable by correlation_id and include failure category (if any).
14) [ ] Note any operator UX pain (confusing errors, missing links) in CLI feedback doc + create follow-up issues.

F) Staging rollback criteria (explicit)
Stop / rollback immediately if any of the below is true:
- A readiness gate is bypassed or can be bypassed unintentionally.
- Routing advertises capacity before Ready, or Ready is set before perf-canary completes.
- Provisioning run is in a retry loop that creates duplicate resources.
- Cluster comes up but validation failures are non-actionable (no clear error + runbook pointer).

Staging rollback actions
- [ ] Pause run:
  - rwctl fleet provision pause --env=staging --run=<run_id>
- [ ] Ensure pool is marked NOT READY in control plane (manual override if needed).
- [ ] Disable feature flag in staging if systemic.
- [ ] File incident-style thread in #eng-infra with correlation_id + links.

================================================================================
PRODUCTION PILOT (internal pool first, then 1 customer expansion)

Production pilot guardrails
- Run during approved change window.
- Start with smallest safe blast radius (internal/prod pool not serving external traffic), then customer expansion.
- Always keep manual override path available; do not proceed if controls (pause/resume, safe re-run) are not working.

A) Pre-prod go/no-go (day-of)
1) [ ] Confirm no ongoing incidents affecting Dedicated provisioning or routing.
2) [ ] Confirm on-point coverage for full window + 60 minutes after.
3) [ ] Confirm dashboards are healthy and alert routing is set per SRE plan (page vs ticket).
4) [ ] Confirm customer success criteria + rollback criteria are documented in SUP ticket (if customer).

B) Enable prod feature flag (only when ready)
5) [ ] Announce in #eng-releases: “Enabling provisioning_pipeline_v2 for prod pilot; pool=<id>; expected duration <X>.”
6) [ ] Flip provisioning_pipeline_v2 = ON for the specific scope agreed (prefer scoped enablement by pool_id if supported).
7) [ ] Confirm flag state in control plane config (screenshot/log line).

C) Prod dry-run + start
8) [ ] Dry-run:
   - rwctl fleet provision run --env=prod --pool=<id> --dry-run
9) [ ] Start run:
   - rwctl fleet provision run --env=prod --pool=<id>
10) [ ] Post correlation_id and dashboard link in #eng-infra + #eng-oncall (single thread).

D) Monitor with required views (prod)
11) Required monitoring tabs (keep open)
   - Dedicated readiness dashboard filtered to pool_id
   - Provisioning runs list (state machine view)
   - Logs for fleet-provisioner service (filter correlation_id)
   - Routing capacity view (confirm no pre-Ready capacity advertised)
   - Perf-canary results view

12) Key SLO-ish checks (pilot)
   - p95 stage durations not wildly outside budget (note: single run ≠ p95, but we still flag gross regressions)
   - Failure categories are actionable (quota/IAM, image mirror, helm values, GPU health)

E) Customer expansion pilot steps (only after internal/prod success)
13) Customer comms
   - [ ] Confirm start time with customer (via CS) and re-state: “capacity will not be routed until Ready; expect validation window where nodes exist but not serving.”
   - [ ] Update SUP ticket with “pilot started” and next update checkpoint.

14) Execution
   - [ ] Trigger expansion for customer pool <customer_pool_id>.
   - [ ] SRE monitors for any spillover: 5xx, routing anomalies, control plane load.

15) Success criteria (customer)
   - [ ] Pool becomes Ready within agreed time budget.
   - [ ] No customer-visible errors attributable to validation window (pool kept out of routing until Ready).
   - [ ] If any pause/resume or stage re-run is used, it is documented in SUP + ENG-2753 with timestamps.

================================================================================
ROLLBACK PLAN (prod) — explicit stop points

Rollback should be treated as normal/expected for a pilot. Prefer early rollback over prolonged “limping.”

Hard rollback triggers (immediate)
- Routing advertises non-Ready capacity.
- Ready state can be reached without passing perf-canary.
- Automation causes duplicate infrastructure creation or leaks resources.
- Validation failures suggest unsafe GPU health (e.g., widespread ECC errors) with unclear containment.

Soft rollback triggers (decision within 10–15 minutes)
- Stage is stuck beyond threshold (e.g., Bootstrapping > 2x expected) with no forward progress.
- Alerts fire indicating increased failure rate across unrelated pools (potential systemic impact).

Rollback actions (prod)
1) [ ] Pause in-flight run(s)
   - rwctl fleet provision pause --env=prod --run=<run_id>
2) [ ] Force pool NOT READY and verify routing excludes it
   - Confirm routing capacity view shows 0 from this pool
3) [ ] Disable provisioning_pipeline_v2 flag (scoped disable preferred; global disable acceptable if systemic)
4) [ ] Revert to manual provisioning path (runbook) for the pool if capacity is still required
5) [ ] Open incident-style thread (or incident if impact) with:
   - correlation_id
   - pool_id
   - last successful stage
   - error category
   - links to logs/dashboards

================================================================================
POST-PILOT CLOSEOUT (both staging + prod)

1) [ ] Write up outcome in ENG-2752 / ENG-2753
   - Actual time-to-ready + stage breakdown
   - Any manual interventions (pause/resume, stage re-run, break-glass)
   - Issues found + links

2) [ ] Update runbooks (same day if possible)
   - Add “most common failure modes” and exact commands used
   - Add screenshots/links to dashboard widgets

3) [ ] Alerting tuning notes (SRE)
   - Were stuck-stage alerts too noisy? Too quiet?
   - Paging vs ticketing boundaries

4) [ ] Resource hygiene
   - Confirm no leaked infra resources
   - Confirm drift detection is clean (or create follow-up)

5) [ ] Retro inputs
   - Add 3 bullets to retro notes doc: what went well / what hurt / what we should automate next

Notes / open questions
- Should we enforce pool-scoped feature flag only for pilots (to avoid accidental global enable)?
- For customer pilots, do we want an automated “customer-facing status page update” step, or keep manual via CS?
- Define “stuck stage” threshold per stage/SKU/region (current values may be too generic).
